title: Incremental POST parsing (retained)
review_status: Retained at 0d41d76; POST 50 latency trade-off accepted. Larger chunks and ijson not retained.
summary: POST tracked peaks −47.4% / −36.3% vs original; POST 50 latency +10.4%. Linux reference RSS separately verified.

cpu.procedure: 3 fresh processes/workload · 1 request · no warm-up. Phase medians: all three; function tables: session 1.
cpu.scope: Imports, startup and first request are separate. Function rows cover all captured phases, including SDK imports.
cpu.reading_guide: Inclusive function CPU overlaps; do not sum it. Raw JSON decoder counts include SDK setup, not only run parsing.
cpu.limitation: Instrumented CPU, not latency. No new paired cold-CPU reduction claim; warmed parser diagnostics are separate.

memory.scope: Whole benchmark-test high-watermark, including fixture generation, repeated execution and GET seeding. Not server RSS.
memory.reading_guide: Median of three recordings; top groups come from an actual median-peak recording and sum to its peak.
memory.limitation: Missing Python stacks limit attribution. Lower GET-test peaks do not establish lower GET-request RAM; its POST seed changed.

server_memory.scope: Assumed Linux/ARM64 · 1 Uvicorn worker · 1 vCPU / 1 GiB · real HTTP · no profiler. Three fresh workers/version/configuration; not a live-production guarantee.

findings.title: Retained memory optimization
findings.interpretation: One run at a time; accept the observed large-batch latency cost. Allocation peaks are not resident RAM.
findings.optimization: Incremental POST parsing · stdlib JSON · 256 KiB max chunks
findings.validation: 10 application + 6 dashboard tests passed; exact measured sources verified

findings.title: Latency trade-off
findings.interpretation: Fresh paired control; three suite medians/version. ~31 ms penalty for POST 50, not a blanket increase across requests.
findings.optimization: Memory goal met; latency penalty not solved
findings.validation: All six original benchmark reports published unchanged

findings.title: Parser CPU diagnosis
findings.evidence: POST 50 preparation: 58.1 → 85.3 CPU ms · 66 incomplete attempts
findings.interpretation: Repeated parsing explains extra CPU. Separate warmed fake-storage diagnostic; not cold-profile latency.
findings.optimization: Diagnose, do not count CPU as a request-latency win
findings.validation: CPU profiles and controlled retry counters retained

findings.title: Rejected parser follow-ups
findings.evidence: 512 KiB / 1 MiB / ijson · not in final code
findings.interpretation: No consistent end-to-end latency win without RAM/behavior costs. Numeric-fix prototype passed 418/421 compatibility checks.
findings.optimization: Keep the measured stdlib memory-saving parser
findings.validation: Original follow-up findings preserved; no new dependency

limitations: No claim of an eliminated latency penalty; production retention depends on its latency SLO.
Memray is whole-test allocation tracing; RSS is server memory in an assumed Linux reference, not an unknown deployment guarantee.
GET is unchanged; its Memray capture includes the changed POST seed.
Follow-ups are rejected experiments, not additional retained optimizations.

metric_sources.rule: Phase medians of three accepted fresh processes; function rows are session 1, all captured phases. No causal CPU claim.
Median of three peaks; groups from the median recording. Alias prepare_runs to create_runs only for the frozen classifier; sums and all 24 recordings verified.
Raw repeats displayed separately. Paired findings use median of three report medians; no rewritten/aggregate benchmark JSON.
Median OS lifetime peak of three fresh workers per version/workload/concurrency. RSS and Memray remain separate series.
Exact source/recording hashes, correctness and preserved follow-up findings; diagnostic CPU is not benchmark latency.
